issues.t: High-voltage battery loses voltage, causing reduced power or no propulsion
issues.sym: A "Propulsion Power is Reduced" or service message, weak acceleration, shorter electric range, or the car suddenly losing drive power or refusing to start.
issues.why: On second-generation Volts, the high-voltage battery or its battery energy control module can fail so the pack can't keep its voltage. GM opened a customer satisfaction program (N202307990) for batteries that gradually lose the ability to hold voltage.
issues.next: If you lose power, move to a safe spot and stop. Ask a Chevrolet dealer to check your VIN for open programs and the 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranty before paying for repairs.

issues.t: "Propulsion Power is Reduced" from battery cell imbalance
issues.sym: A "Propulsion Power is Reduced" message, slower acceleration, and less electric range than before.
issues.why: Groups of cells in the high-voltage battery can drift out of balance or drop to low voltage. GM addressed this through service bulletins and a customer satisfaction program (17228) for affected cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer scan the hybrid system and check for open campaigns. Battery section repairs are often covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranty.

issues.t: Software update may stop battery cell balancing (recall)
issues.sym: A reduced-power message and, in the worst case, loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: A control module update could switch off cell balancing in the high-voltage battery, letting cells get too low and cut propulsion.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: "Shift to Park" message won't let the car turn off
issues.sym: The car is in Park but the screen says "Shift to Park," and it won't fully power down. You may have to wiggle the shifter, and the 12V battery can drain if the car stays on.
issues.why: A switch in the shifter that tells the car it is in Park can give a false signal. GM issued several bulletins on this, ending with repair bulletin 19-NA-206.
issues.next: Try moving the shifter firmly into Park again. A dealer can install the fix from the bulletin; if it is out of warranty, ask about any goodwill coverage.

issues.t: Shifter hard to move into or out of Park
issues.sym: The shift lever feels stiff, sticks, or is hard to move in or out of Park.
issues.why: GM found a burr on a spring inside the shifter of some 2016-2017 Volts (bulletin 43940) and issued a repair procedure for the knob, cable and shifter (16-NA-060).
issues.next: Do not force it. Have a dealer inspect the shifter and apply the bulletin repair.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains and car won't power on
issues.sym: The car won't turn on, the screens stay dark, or the doors and charge port won't respond, even though the big battery has charge.
issues.why: Like a regular car, the Volt needs a healthy 12-volt battery to power up. Weak 12-volt batteries, modules that keep running while parked, or a failing power converter that charges the 12-volt battery can leave it flat.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and charged. If it keeps going flat, ask a shop to check for a parasitic drain and test the accessory power module.

issues.t: Gas engine may auto-start in a closed garage (recall)
issues.sym: The car is left "on" after you walk away, and later the gas engine starts by itself to charge the battery, filling a closed garage with exhaust.
issues.why: If the car was not fully switched off, the battery could drain enough that the engine started on its own. GM updated the software so the car shuts itself off.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Whining noise from the drive unit
issues.sym: A whine from under the car that rises and falls with speed.
issues.why: The drive unit (the Volt's transmission and motors) can develop a whine, with a 2012 average around 84,000 miles.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the drive unit fluid and listen to the noise. Whines that get louder over time should be checked before they turn into a bearing failure.

issues.t: Power steering cuts out while driving
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets heavy while driving, often with a warning message.
issues.why: This is the most reported problem on the 2017 Volt, and it is one of the more expensive repairs on this car. GM also issued bulletins to inspect the steering gear (16-NA-109).
issues.next: Slow down and steer firmly if assist drops out. Have a dealer read the steering codes and inspect the steering gear.

issues.t: Infotainment screen freezes or fails
issues.sym: The center touchscreen freezes, goes blank, reboots, or stops responding.
issues.why: Infotainment failure is the second most reported problem on 2017 Volts, averaging about 29,000 miles.
issues.next: Try a full shutdown and restart. Ask a dealer for any software update before replacing the radio or display.

issues.t: Loss of propulsion or no-start from loose high-voltage connection
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power or won't start, often with several warning messages.
issues.why: GM found that a high-voltage fuse might not be tightened properly (16NA193), and that a high-voltage interlock connector could sink into its fuse block cover (16185).
issues.next: Do not open high-voltage parts yourself. Have a dealer check for these bulletins and campaigns.

issues.t: Check engine light and lost regen when pressing both pedals
issues.sym: A check engine light and less regenerative braking after the brake and gas pedals were pressed at the same time.
issues.why: GM bulletin 16NA256 covers this software behavior.
issues.next: Avoid pressing both pedals at once. A dealer can clear the code and apply any update.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or the passenger airbag status shows off with an adult seated.
issues.why: The sensor mat in the passenger seat can bunch and fold, raising its resistance so the system faults. NHTSA looked into this, and GM offered repairs without a recall.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The passenger airbag may not work while the light is on, so get it fixed and ask a dealer whether GM will cover it.

issues.t: Front brakes may not release during ABS or traction control (recall)
issues.sym: During an ABS, stability or traction event, a front brake could stay applied, pulling the car or locking a wheel.
issues.why: A faulty valve in the brake pressure modulator on some 2012 cars built in March-April 2012 might not release front brake pressure.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Inner tie rod may separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking, loose or wandering steering, and in the worst case loss of steering on one wheel.
issues.why: On some cars built on April 11, 2014, the inner tie rod may not have been tightened properly to the steering gear.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag may inflate improperly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a high-speed crash, the driver's airbag might not inflate correctly in its second stage.
issues.why: A defect in the driver's frontal airbag module could cause improper second-stage inflation.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the inflator could burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect could let the driver's airbag inflator rupture when it deploys.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Rear brake calipers may reduce braking (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or spongy brake pedal and longer stopping distances.
issues.why: Some rear caliper pistons were not coated properly, letting gas pockets form in the brake system.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Rear seatbelt may not lock for child seats (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seatbelt doesn't lock when pulled all the way out to secure a child seat.
issues.why: Some rear seatbelt retractors may not switch into their locking mode.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Windshield washer pump stops working
issues.sym: No washer fluid sprays when you pull the washer switch, though the reservoir is full.
issues.why: The washer pump can fail and is one of the problems RepairPal lists for the Volt.
issues.next: Check the fuse and hoses first. The pump is usually an easy and inexpensive part to replace.

issues.t: Power window stops or falls into the door
issues.sym: A front window moves slowly, makes grinding noises, stops partway, or drops into the door.
issues.why: The window regulator cables can tangle or break, which RepairPal reports on the Volt.
issues.next: Have the regulator replaced; the motor can often be reused if it still works.
